name: Bifrost Java CodeQL quality
description: Public Java declaration, naming, generics, constructor, and Javadoc quality policies aligned with reviewed CodeQL query identities and engine fact contracts.

policies.severity_rationale: A field that is only assigned during initialization can be final, making the class invariant explicit.
policies.remediation: Declare initialization-only immutable fields final after reviewing subclassing and serialization requirements.

policies.severity_rationale: An unused non-private field exposes mutable state beyond the type boundary.
policies.remediation: Make the field private or document and preserve the required external access contract.

policies.severity_rationale: Static final constants with lowercase names obscure their constant role and weaken naming consistency.
policies.remediation: Rename the constant using the project’s uppercase constant convention, preserving API compatibility where required.

policies.severity_rationale: Uppercase-initial variable declarations look like types or constants and make local data flow harder to read.
policies.remediation: Rename fields, parameters, and locals with a lowercase initial according to the project naming convention.

policies.severity_rationale: A single underscore is reserved or invalid as a Java identifier in modern source levels.
policies.remediation: Replace the underscore declaration or package segment with a descriptive identifier.

policies.severity_rationale: Using the keyword enum as an identifier is invalid or confusing Java syntax.
policies.remediation: Rename the declaration to a non-keyword identifier.

policies.severity_rationale: A method named like its enclosing type is easy to mistake for a constructor but has different method semantics.
policies.remediation: Rename the method or make the declaration a real constructor with the intended initialization behavior.

policies.severity_rationale: Constructing a generic type without type arguments discards compile-time type safety.
policies.remediation: Supply the intended generic type arguments, preferably using the diamond operator where appropriate.

policies.severity_rationale: A raw generic return type weakens callers’ type checking and can introduce unchecked conversions.
policies.remediation: Return the generic type with its intended type arguments.

policies.severity_rationale: A raw generic field, local, or parameter weakens the type contract at the declaration boundary.
policies.remediation: Add the intended type arguments to the field, local, or parameter declaration.

policies.severity_rationale: A type variable or wildcard bound that extends a final type cannot admit a meaningful subtype.
policies.remediation: Use an open bound or remove the unnecessary type parameter after reviewing the API contract.

policies.severity_rationale: A type parameter that shadows a visible type name makes signatures and references ambiguous to readers.
policies.remediation: Rename the type parameter so the visible type remains unambiguous.

policies.severity_rationale: An impossible checked-exception Javadoc tag documents behavior the callable does not declare.
policies.remediation: Remove the stale tag or update the declaration and documentation to describe the actual checked exception contract.

policies.severity_rationale: A Javadoc parameter tag that names no callable or type parameter is stale documentation.
policies.remediation: Rename the tag to a declared parameter or remove it.

policies.severity_rationale: A public callable’s checked exception contract is incomplete without an acceptable Javadoc throws tag.
policies.remediation: Document each declared checked exception with an accurate @throws or @exception tag.

policies.severity_rationale: Public callable behavior is harder to use and review when it has no Javadoc contract.
policies.remediation: Add a Javadoc block describing the callable’s behavior, parameters, return value, and exceptions as applicable.

policies.severity_rationale: A public callable parameter without Javadoc leaves its input contract unspecified.
policies.remediation: Add an accurate @param tag for each eligible public parameter.

policies.severity_rationale: A public non-void callable without a return-value description leaves callers without an output contract.
policies.remediation: Add an accurate @return tag describing the returned value.

policies.severity_rationale: A public source type without Javadoc leaves its purpose and contract unexplained.
policies.remediation: Add a Javadoc block describing the public type and its intended use.

policies.severity_rationale: An overriding or implementing method without an Override annotation loses compiler checks and makes the inheritance contract harder to read.
policies.remediation: Add @Override to the overriding or implementing method after checking its superclass or interface contract.
